claims.wording: Trace is a Mac storage inspector and app uninstaller.
claims.excerpt: Trace is a storage inspector and app uninstaller. It shows disk usage, file associations, and risks so you can make informed choices.

claims.wording: Trace requires macOS 15 or later and supports Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
claims.excerpt: Trace requires macOS 15 or later and supports both Apple silicon and Intel Macs.
claims.conditions: Vendor support statement, no architecture testing performed.

claims.wording: The documented download is Trace 2.0.1, build 61; the guide dates that release September 23, 2026.
claims.excerpt: Trace 2.0.1 (61) September 23, 2026
claims.conditions: Download link and release list only; installer not downloaded or executed; not proof no other release channel exists.

claims.wording: The demo analyzes storage and associations; Trace Agent, including its removal actions, is free. A licence unlocks other paid actions.
claims.excerpt: Use the demo to analyze storage and review file associations. Trace Agent is fully usable for free, including removal actions. A license unlocks the other paid actions.

claims.wording: Trace uses a commercial EULA; future major upgrades may require a new purchase, despite continued use of the licensed version.
claims.excerpt: A new major version or a new product may be offered as a separate upgrade and may require a new purchase or a separate license.
additionalExcerpts: You are granted a non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable license to install and use the Software in accordance with the license type specified at purchase.
If you have purchased a license, you may generally continue to use the licensed version indefinitely.
claims.conditions: Do not promise lifetime major upgrades; no open-source licence verified.

claims.wording: The provider is Argon Analytik, Inh. Meyer-Wildhagen, a Swiss sole proprietorship.
claims.excerpt: Argon Analytik, Inh. Meyer‑Wildhagen (sole proprietorship, Switzerland)

claims.wording: Trace says storage analysis is local; licensing communicates with Keygen and updates use servers.
claims.excerpt: Trace analyzes storage locally on your Mac. The app does not send usage data for analytics.
additionalExcerpts: If you use licensing, Trace communicates with the licensing service (Keygen) for activation/validation.
Updates are technically downloaded from a server
claims.conditions: Policy statement, not network audit. Do not say entirely offline or zero network access; activation/validation may need internet.

claims.wording: Trace documents exact and heuristic app/file associations, risk labels and shared-data warnings.
claims.excerpt: Each entry shows a Match badge (for example Exact/Heuristic), risk level (safe/caution/danger), and a “Why?” explanation.
claims.conditions: Vendor labels are not a guarantee data can be removed safely.

claims.wording: Four cleanup presets set default selections; individual paths can be changed, and shared data is not selected by default.
claims.excerpt: Trace offers four presets that only control the default selection. You can always select/deselect individual paths manually.
additionalExcerpts: Data shared by multiple apps (e.g. Microsoft Office, Adobe) is marked as “Shared/Danger” and is never selected by default in any preset.
claims.conditions: Cache, Associations, App, Everything; Everything can remove user data. Not hands-on validation.

claims.wording: Quarantine is explicitly chosen, retains data on disk and frees no space at that stage; permanent removal cannot be undone.
claims.excerpt: Quarantine is an option you explicitly choose, not the default for every Delete button. The data stays on disk in a session that records its original location. No space is freed at this stage.
additionalExcerpts: Only permanent removal releases the occupied space; it cannot be undone.
claims.conditions: Do not promise exact reclaimed bytes; APFS/shared allocation complicates that relationship.

claims.wording: TraceAgent offers reviewed app-leftover selections; its Delete action moves selected data to Trash, not permanent deletion.
claims.excerpt: TraceAgent never deletes anything automatically and is free to use in the demo too.
additionalExcerpts: The agent’s Delete action moves selected data to the Trash. It does not delete it permanently

claims.wording: The Watcher records changed areas for rechecking; it is not a continuous full scan or automatic deletion system.
claims.excerpt: The Watcher detects filesystem changes and records which areas need another check. Valid saved results can be reused on the next launch. It does not run a continuous full scan or delete anything automatically.
claims.conditions: Not proof of a recurring-growth timeline or CPU/process-helper grouping.

claims.wording: Full Disk Access and background service permissions affect coverage; privileged helper actions need separate consideration.
claims.excerpt: Background activity and Full Disk Access are different permissions. An enabled agent does not automatically gain access to protected data.
additionalExcerpts: For certain features, Trace may require additional macOS permissions (e.g. Full Disk Access) or a privileged helper (e.g. for system-wide actions).
claims.conditions: No installation performed; signing/notarization independently unverified; never advise bypassing protections.

claims.wording: Trace documents development storage categories and Homebrew package uninstall through brew uninstall.
claims.excerpt: In the Development category details, the Homebrew tab lists installed formulae and casks and lets you uninstall individual packages via brew uninstall with live output.
claims.conditions: Coverage list includes Xcode, npm, Gradle, Maven, Cargo and other paths; recognition does not make all contents disposable or certify every adapter.

claims.wording: tracectl is a read-only companion, not an unattended deletion interface.
claims.excerpt: tracectl is Trace's read-only command-line companion.
additionalExcerpts: Mutating actions such as delete, Quarantine, restore, or helper repair stay in the app with visible confirmation.

claims.wording: Trace documents a recent Time Machine check for permanent deletion at caution, high or unknown risk, not for every action.
claims.excerpt: The additional Time Machine check applies to permanent deletion with caution, high, or unknown risk. A confirmed backup from the last 24 hours counts as current.
claims.conditions: Vendor-documented, not tested; a recent backup does not guarantee inclusion of every file.

claims.wording: Allocated size is not automatically reclaimable space because hard links and APFS clones can share storage.
claims.excerpt: Hard links and APFS clones can share storage. An allocated size is therefore not automatically the amount that deleting that item would reclaim.
claims.conditions: Attributed documentation explanation; no measured savings.

claims.wording: Breathing Room, which we build, is a free Apache-2.0 macOS maintenance preview with optional hosted AI Care advertised at USD 5/month or USD 50/year.
claims.excerpt: Breathing Room is a free, Apache-2.0 macOS maintenance preview

workflow.title: Review Mac app leftovers without confusing quarantine with free space
workflow.primaryIntent: Understand app association evidence, shared-data warnings and the different consequences of quarantine, Trash and permanent removal.
workflow.leadDirection: Conclusion first: review ownership and recoverability before deciding to remove; quarantine keeps data on disk and is not a reclaimed-space result. No hands-on claim.
sections: Inspect the app's associated files, not just its bundle size (T09)
Separate shared data from app-only leftovers (T10)
Distinguish allocated bytes from expected recovery (T18)
Choose storage/uninstall inspection or ongoing process/activity investigation (B01,B02)
workflow.visualPlan: Required official Trace app screenshot after lead only when reuse cleared; current-source labeled Breathing Room Space preview later at workflow-choice point. Additional link-only quarantine example: https://trace.argio.ch/assets/screenshots/en/additional/dashboard-quarantine.webp from guide #quarantaene; rights also unresolved.
workflow.interactionPass: Hand off a non-mutating decision checklist: ownership established? shared? backed up? restoration needed? It must never label a real path safe or calculate promised savings. No filesystem access or cleanup execution.
workflow.distinctness: Mechanism-led workflow on quarantine retaining bytes and app-leftover review, not a longer copy of the product comparison.

comparison.title: Breathing Room vs Trace for macOS
comparison.primaryIntent: Choose between documented app/file association and uninstall review versus a maintenance preview's process/activity and hosted-assistance workflow.
structure: Bounded choice with 'Breathing Room, which we build' disclosure
When Trace fits; when Breathing Room fits
Preview/runtime, permissions, pricing and unverified cells
traceAdvantages: Documented app/file match explanations, shared-data risk labels and explicit quarantine review (T09–T11)
One-time licensed-version use rather than assuming a recurring subscription (T04,T06)
traceTradeoffs: macOS 15 minimum vs Breathing Room's advertised macOS 13 preview minimum (T02,B01)
Quarantine retains bytes; irreversible deletion and APFS accounting require care (T11,T18)
Some actions paid; VAT extra; future major upgrades may need purchase (T04–T06)
Process grouping and a recurring-growth timeline not verified; never mark No

Hosted assistance needs authentication/internet and relevant diagnostic data transfer; not all-local AI (B02)
Daily care must run while app is open and uses saved approvals; not arbitrary unattended deletion (B02)
